name.value: What happens to my work?

Your chats, project titles, notes, finished scripts, and story profile are saved to your Studio account so you can return to them. When you ask StorySculpt to continue or revise, your title, profile, notes, and recent messages are processed by the AI model that writes your next question or draft, guided by David's method and your own words. Do not enter anything you do not want processed by an AI service.

name.value: Can I change the format?
The format is locked after creation. Start a new script to use a different format; your existing chat stays in your list.

name.value: Can I pause and come back?

value.value: Can I pause and come back?

name.value: Yes. Leaving does not delete your project. Reopen the chat to resume the interview where you stopped. Check the save indicator before closing the browser: Saving means a write is pending, Saved means it was acknowledged, and Not saved means the latest change has not reached your account yet. Changes kept only on this device are not available on another device until saved.

name.value: What does finishing a script mean?

value.value: What does finishing a script mean?

name.value: Finishing closes the interview to new turns and assembles your answers into a script you can record. Once a script is finished, the interview is locked so your script stays stable. A new answer cannot be added to a finished interview; use Refine with a note to change the script, or start a new chat for your next script. Copy it or download the text file when you are ready to film. Your saved script does not expire; it stays in your account until you delete it.

name.value: How long does an interview take?

value.value: How long does an interview take?

name.value: An interview takes about 5 to 10 minutes across 4 to 6 conversational turns. You talk through raw, unedited thoughts one question at a time in your natural phrasing, without needing an outline, slide deck, or prepared notes. Rough answers give the 5E framework the real emotional tension and personal perspective your video needs.

name.value: What happens after my first script?

value.value: What happens after my first script?

name.value: When your first script is finished, it is ready to record. You can copy it directly to your teleprompter or download the text file to film your video. Once you film, mark it filmed or start your next script to build momentum. Your saved scripts stay in your library and your standing story profile carries forward what StorySculpt learned about your voice and audience into every new script you create.

name.value: Can I archive or delete a chat?

value.value: Can I archive or delete a chat?

name.value: Leaving pauses your chat; it does not delete anything. Check that your changes say Saved before closing the browser. Archive puts a chat away without deleting its notes, answers or script. Use the Archive button beside its title, then open Archived and choose Restore chat to bring it back to All. Delete is different: after you confirm, it permanently removes the chat, its versions, and its saved script.

name.value: What happens when I delete a project?

value.value: What happens when I delete a project?

name.value: Deleting a project permanently removes the chat, its recorded versions, and the finished script. When you delete a chat, you get a short undo window of about ten seconds where the row shows Deleted and an Undo button to restore it immediately. After that window lapses, the server delete runs and the work is permanently gone. Returning after a delete shows your remaining active chats, or the clean start screen if you have no other chats.
